account:
Today has been mostly routine mayoral business, but several matters remain unclear. At the town accounts appointment, the secretary had received no figures, correspondence, or payment requests. The appointments chest held the appointment book, and the secretary later found no accounts on any of the four great hall tables. I inspected the treasury: 128 emeralds, which I left untouched. We do not know who holds the financial ledger; the secretary has filed a request and is keeping it pending. This is a records problem, not evidence of missing money.

At tea, my neighbour repeated vague talk of lights or some change near the bridge or port, without concrete details. The secretary says no plans or requests for work there have reached the office. I have not personally seen such work and cannot say what the talk refers to.

The secretary reported that the builder was looking for the innkeeper about supplies. Earlier I heard townsfolk say the baker carried a sack of bread at the inn; my neighbour also said the baker intended to stock the market with fresh bread. These could be ordinary provisioning. I do not know of a connection between them or the riverside rumours.

The innkeeper has now requested my presence precisely at eighteen o'clock tomorrow in the great hall, asking the secretary to record the meeting and escort me on time. I have confirmed it. He describes it as an innkeeper's community hospitality matter and says to bring only myself, with no preparation needed. His emphasis on timing and attendance is noticeable, but the stated purpose is hospitality; I have no evidence of any other purpose. The secretary is currently holding the appointment book, apparently checking or updating it. I should keep tomorrow's meeting as well as my other appointments.
